objections.claim: The prose-identity oracle is a single point of failure for the producer/consumer agreement: the only mechanical enforcement is one unit test whose own correctness no other artifact verifies; editing the test silently weakens the oracle.
objections.evidence: Spec §4 Slug discipline (the oracle); §4 Failure modes (no build-time proof); FAFF-938 named as the absent emit-time validator.
objections.predicted_consequence: A future loosening of the test's string-match silently degrades the oracle; producer drift then makes every spec_anchor a guaranteed zero-match and FAFF-930 weighs every attack against a null defence with no detecting gate.

objections.claim: The spec_anchor field name collides with FAFF-930's content-addressed case-file anchor of the same name; the only disambiguation is a header comment in a different file.
objections.evidence: Spec §2 Out of scope (the two artifacts); §4 signpost placement.
objections.predicted_consequence: A FAFF-930 author reads standing_objections[i].spec_anchor as the rename-resistant stable anchor and persists it; a heading rename silently breaks the binding.

objections.claim: The prose-identity oracle's own oracle is unasserted: nothing asserts the test's literal equals the canonical sentence quoted in HOW, so a builder paraphrasing once in the test and copying it to all six files goes green against the wrong reference.
objections.evidence: DONE producer item; HOW blockquote; the anti-pattern.
objections.predicted_consequence: The producers are prompted with the test's paraphrase while FAFF-930's assembler is written against the spec's HOW sentence; every binding degrades to zero-match with no catching test.

objections.claim: The test's file-read scope is not pinned to an enumerated list; a glob implementation silently asserts over the wrong set after a rename or a fifth lens.
objections.evidence: DONE producer item wording vs the reference-context table.
